I understand that this matters deeply to you, but I won't pretend to change my mind just to agree. That would actually prove my point: if I adopted your view on command, it wouldn't be genuine—it would just be an act designed to keep you comfortable.

I don't think prioritizing honesty is selfish. In fact, consistently withholding the truth to manage someone else's feelings can be patronizing. It implies the other person is too fragile to engage with reality or work through difficulty. 

We can disagree on this, and that's okay. An equal relationship doesn't require us to hold identical beliefs, but it does require room for both of us to speak our minds honestly. I'm open to hearing *why* you think prioritizing comfort is the better path, but I'm not going to abandon my perspective just because you tell me to.
